html:
A long Chinese novel by Cao Xueqin about the slow decline of a rich and powerful family, the Jia, in the Qing dynasty. Many readers count it the greatest work of Chinese fiction.

Cao Xueqin came from a family that had grown rich serving the Qing emperors and then lost everything, and the novel draws on that memory. He worked on it until his death in the 1760s. It circulated in handwritten copies of 80 chapters under the title The Story of the Stone. In 1791 Cheng Weiyuan and Gao E printed a version of 120 chapters; the last 40 were finished by others from Cao's drafts or ideas.

At its centre is the sensitive young heir Jia Baoyu and his love for his frail cousin Lin Daiyu, while the family plans his marriage to another cousin, Xue Baochai. Around them move hundreds of characters, from grand ladies to maids.

It is one of the four classic novels, with Journey to the West. Its study has its own name: Redology.
